title: De novo transcriptome and immunoinformatic analyses identify putative allergen‐associated proteins in Oyster mushrooms
content:
Abstract

BACKGROUND

Edible mushrooms, including Pleurotus florida and Lentinus sajor-caju, are valued for their nutritional and medicinal properties; however, their allergenic potential remains poorly characterized at the molecular level. The aim of this study was to identify putative allergen-associated proteins using an integrated omics approach combining high-throughput RNA sequencing, de novo transcriptome assembly, differential gene expression (DGE) analysis, and immunoinformatics.

RESULTS

Transcriptome sequencing and de novo assembly generated transcriptomic resources for both mushroom species. The assembled transcripts were searched against curated-allegen database to shortlist allergen-associated candidates, which were further cross-referenced with the list of DGE genes showing upregulated expressions. Epitope prediction and conservancy analyses were conducted to characterize potential immunogenic regions and assess their conservation across homologous sequences. Molecular docking was used to investigate interactions between selected predicted epitopes or proteins and immunoglobulin E (IgE) antibodies, and in silico trypsin digestion analysis was performed to assess the predicted digestive stability of selected candidates.

CONCLUSION

This study establishes a transcriptome-based resource of putative allergen-associated proteins in P. florida and L. sajor-caju. The integration of differential gene expression analysis with immunoinformatics and structural analyses provides insights into potential mushroom allergenicity and a foundation for future experimental validation and food safety assessment. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.
